articles.title: ‘India national team is not Indian cricket’: Sunil Gavaskar’s strong message to BCCI and ICC
articles.summary: Cricket News: Sunil Gavaskar has sounded a warning over the relentless demands being placed on Indian cricketers, calling for a rethink of the packed international .
articles.body: Sunil Gavaskar has sounded a warning over the relentless demands being placed on Indian cricketers, calling for a rethink of the packed international calendar and greater emphasis on the domestic game.The former India captain has cautioned against sending players from one series or tournament to another without giving them adequate time to recover. His comments, made in his Sportstar column, come amid growing concerns over the workload on India's players and a recent spate of injuries.A week ago, BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia had attributed the injury problems affecting Indian cricket to the team's heavy match schedule. The board is now keen to find a solution to the issue.With the ICC preparing to discuss the next four-year international calendar cycle beginning in 2027, Gavaskar believes the strain on players needs to be considered while the schedule is being framed.Gavaskar’s warning over player workloadGavaskar referred to the recent meeting held to take stock of Indian cricket and hoped the concerns surrounding the workload would also be reflected in discussions at the ICC.“The recent meeting to take stock of Indian cricket did try to come to grips with the issue. Hopefully, when the ICC meeting to discuss the international cricket calendar over the next cycle of four years from 2027 takes place, the decision-makers will realise that Indian cricketers are neither machines nor sugarcane to be endlessly squeezed for every drop of the juice,” Gavaskar wrote in his column.The former batter's comments come at a time when India's leading players are required to navigate a packed schedule across formats and competitions, increasing the physical demands on an already stretched group.‘The India cricket team is not Indian cricket’Gavaskar also believes the conversation around Indian cricket needs to extend beyond the senior national team.While India's international side remains the most visible part of the sport in the country, he argued that it is ultimately produced by a much wider domestic ecosystem and should not be viewed as synonymous with Indian cricket itself.“The India cricket team is not Indian cricket,” he wrote. “The India cricket team is the by-product of Indian cricket.”For Gavaskar, that distinction is particularly relevant when discussions turn to India's much-praised bench strength.Gavaskar questions India’s three-team depthIndia's ability to field several sides with international experience has often been cited as evidence of the country's enormous talent pool. Gavaskar, however, believes that having enough players to assemble multiple teams does not necessarily mean the domestic system is consistently producing world-class cricketers.He pointed to recent results as a reason to look beyond the perception of India's extraordinary depth and focus instead on strengthening the system that feeds the national team.“The argument that India’s bench strength is such that it can field three teams is good to make claims for the world, but the reality, as recent results have shown, is that one India team is at the moment not good enough to win much silverware. Yes, a gold in the Asian Games will once again rejuvenate the team and give it the confidence for oncoming battles, but unless domestic cricket is prioritised, the pipeline will not produce world beaters. All the best to both our boys and girls to win the gold,” Gavaskar wrote.Gavaskar's argument, therefore, goes beyond simply reducing the workload of India's established stars. He believes the long-term health of Indian cricket depends equally on ensuring that domestic cricket remains strong enough to continually produce players capable of succeeding at the highest level.As the ICC prepares to map out the international calendar from 2027 onwards, Gavaskar's comments put two connected issues under the spotlight: how much cricket India's players are being asked to play and whether the domestic structure is strong enough to sustain the national team in the years ahead.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Jasprit Bumrah fit, Harshit Rana out: BCCI fires physio ahead of Afghanistan T20Is
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: The T20I team had its first practice session at the Ferozeshah Kotla on Thursday afternoon ahead of the three-match series against Afghanis.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The T20I team had its first practice session at the Ferozeshah Kotla on Thursday afternoon ahead of the three-match series against Afghanistan starting on Sunday.After months of rehab at the Centre of Excellence (CoE), Jasprit Bumrah and Nitish Kumar Reddy were declared fit to join the team which will fly to Japan for the Asian Games two days after the series.Also on Thursday morning, the Indian cricket board (BCCI) announced that Harshit Rana had suffered another injury during his match simulation test at the CoE on Tuesday. Pacer Yash Thakur was named as his replacement.The recurring injuries have become a roadblock for the team management and selection committee as they try to firm up the preparation for next year’s ODI World Cup in southern Africa.It has emerged that the Indian cricket board (BCCI) has decided to let go of Team India physio Kamlesh Jain in the wake of frequent injuries. TOI had reported on Aug 6 that BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia had pulled up Jain for the spate of injuries to top players.The depth in Indian cricket allows India to make multiple T20I teams. It’s the ODI format that has become a headache for the team management.There has been some disagreement in BCCI circles about sending a full-strength T20I team for the Asiad while there are ODIs lined up against West Indies.Even as Abhishek Sharma and Sanju Samson went through their batting sessions in the practice area, head coach Gautam Gambhir was seen spending more time with T20I captain Shreyas Iyer and Washington Sundar — two integral members of the ODI team — when they were batting at the centre square.When the ODI series against West Indies starts in Thiruvananthapuram on Sept 27, Gambhir will be without first-choice ODI players like Bumrah, Iyer, Washington, Axar Patel, Ishan Kishan and Reddy.There’s no clarity about when allrounder Hardik Pandya will be available even as he undergoes an unending rehab at the CoE.While the World Cup may seem a year away, the number of ODIs are few and far between. It has left very little breathing space for the team management and the selectors to firm up the ODI core team.Meanwhile, India’s fast bowling coach Morne Morkel hasn’t yet joined the team. Sources said he is yet to receive his visa renewal.First T20I to go ahead despite traffic police request to rescheduleThe Delhi and District Cricket Association (DDCA) said that the first T20I on Sept 13 will go ahead as scheduled even as the Delhi traffic police wrote a letter to the association requesting to move the match in light of the BRICS summit.In a letter, the DCP (traffic) said the summit would require extensive traffic arrangements, including VVIP/VIP route regulation and deployment of personnel.However, DDCA later posted on X saying the match was on.“The 1st T20I will go ahead as scheduled. Following a meeting with Delhi traffic police, DDCA has been assured of all support,” the association said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 49ers TE injury vs. Rams ‘wasn’t good’ per Kyle Shanahan
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers beat the Los Angeles Rams 27-7 on Thursday night, but they may have lost a tight end for a while.
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers beat the Los Angeles Rams 27-7 at Melbourne Cricket Ground on Thursday night to improve to 1-0 on the season, but during the game, they lost a key player who caught five touchdowns last year.

In the second quarter, 49ers tight end Jake Tonges suffered a knee injury, and trainers had to cart him back to the locker room. While he was questionable to return, he didn't play another snap in the victory.

After the game, 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan didn't have the best injury update.

"It wasn't good," Shanahan said. "It's not ACL. It's MCL, I believe. But there are some issues with it that we gotta see how it is. There's a little more information to it, but we don't know yet."

With George Kittle easing back into action after returning quickly from a torn Achilles, the 49ers might have to rely on him more going forward. They also have Luke Farrell on the 53-man roster and both Brayden Willis and Khalil Dinkins on the practice squad at the position.
